title: Author event and film screening - Thursday at The Bookplate - NewsBreak
text:
By SUBMITTED NEWS ,
20 hours ago
CHESTERTOWN — The Bookplate welcomes a new author event featuring author and academy-award winner Ernest Thompson, discussing his new novel, “Out Clause”, and presenting an intimate screening of his short film, “The Constituent”. The talk will be held on Thursday, May 7 at 6 p.m. in the Sultana Education Foundation’s Holt Center on Cross Street.
What if you could leave your life? An unhappily married CEO jumps from a Connecticut bridge, body never found. A troubled flight attendant still mourning her lover lost on 9/11 goes missing from a cruise ship. An Arizona school teacher can’t reconcile the sexual compromise he’s been maneuvered into and steals money from a student kiosk and disappears. An internet sensation crosses the last line left and self-pleasures in front of an audience of millions and is spotted in Virginia boarding a hot air balloon that’s empty when it crash lands. 500,000 Americans go missing every year, 1500 never return. Where are they and is there a connection? Yes.
Welcome to “Out Clause”.
Written and directed by On Golden Pond Academy Award-winner Ernest Thompson, the short film, The Constituent is adapted from his one-act play by the same name. In it, Chas Potter, a small-town New Hampshire voter, for decades has written no-holds-barred letters to his senator in Washington, D.C. The content of his missives may be more profane than profound but there’s no mistaking the constituent’s patriotic concern, culminating in an uproarious confrontation when the senator has finally had enough and comes calling.
Filmed on a paper-thin budget on location in rural New Hampshire, The Constituent stars two veteran theatre, film, and television actors, Ernest Thompson and NYPD Blue Emmy-winner Gordon Clapp, with a lovely and tender cameo by Ernest’s frequent costar Lisa Bostnar.
Thompson’s work has won an Academy Award, two Golden Globes, Writers Guild and Broadway Drama Guild Awards and been nominated for a Tony, an Emmy and a British Academy Award. His plays have been seen in theatres around the world, his most enduring, On Golden Pond, translated into 30 languages and presented in more than 40 countries.
Current projects include an On Golden Pond Broadway revival, directed by and starring the author, true also of his new one-man play, Archie Parish’s Parting Words, now on tour in the Northeast, the short film The Constituent, and the long-awaited sequel, Home On Golden Pond.
With his writer wife Kerrin Thompson, he established Rescind Recidivism, a prison writing program giving inmates a chance to feel creative as well as human, capable and worthy.
For more event details contact The Bookplate at 410-778-4167 or contact@thebookplate.net. These events are free and open to the public, but reservations are strongly recommended. Sultana’s Holt Education Center is located at 200 S. Cross Street in Chestertown.
